title: Throughput-smoothing mediator for tenant fairness and cold-KV preservation
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem:
We observe tenant unfairness during sustained continuous-batching workloads: aggressive batching and preemption reduce per-token GPU cost but cause repeated cold-KV evictions for low-traffic tenants, increasing their latency tail and producing visible customer regressions. Current preemption policies focus on immediate throughput/latency SLOs and do not explicitly preserve KV residency for low-QPS tenants.

Goal:
Design, implement, and validate a runtime mediator that smooths throughput allocations across tenants to improve fairness while preserving cold-KV residency. The mediator should: (1) avoid oscillatory preemption cycles that thrash KV sets, (2) respect tenant SLO tiers (latency and P99 targets), (3) maintain overall GPU utilization and per-token cost targets, and (4) be configurable via runtime knobs and observable in the Console.

Non-goals:
- Replace global scheduler; this is a per-node mediator that augments the existing preemption stack.
- Solve every cross-node KV migration scenario (out of scope for this ticket).

Design overview:
- Throughput Smoothing Mediator (TSM): lightweight component that sits between admission and preemption. On each admission epoch it computes a per-tenant smoothing credit based on recent sustained throughput, recent preemption events, and a cold-KV penalty term.
- Cold-KV preservation: TSM tracks a moving fingerprint of per-tenant KV working-set residency (hot fraction estimate). Tenants whose hot_fraction < cold_threshold receive a soft-preservation boost that reduces their admissible preemptable quota for a time window, preventing immediate eviction of cached KV lines.
- Progressive fair throttles: combine tenant SLO tier (SLA weight) with a velocity term. Tenants that recently experienced preemption get a temporary elevated weight to restore their throughput quota gradually instead of all at once.
- Memory-aware admission: admission checks include an estimated post-batch KV memory footprint; if the admission would cause eviction pressure above a configured kv_pressure_limit, TSM signals the preemptor to prefer draining high-throughput tenants first but respecting the preservation boost.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive preservation increases overall GPU memory pressure and can reduce utilization. We mitigate this by allowing controlled decay of preservation boosts and a hard kv_pressure_limit that will still permit evictions when required to meet platform SLOs.
- Estimating hot_fraction is noisy at small sample sizes. We use an exponentially weighted moving average with conservative alpha and require a minimum sample window before applying preservation.

Acceptance criteria:
- P99 latency for low-QPS tenants improves by >= 20% in the microbench cold-KV scenario (local perf lab).
- Overall GPU utilization drop <= 5% compared to baseline continuous-batching config under mixed workloads in staging.
- No increase in error-rate or failed batches caused by mediator interventions.
- Console exposes a per-tenant preservation metric and an event log for mediator decisions.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (experiment): add TSM prototype with flags to enable preservation boost and smoothing. Implement telemetry hooks (preservation_score, hot_fraction_estimate, rejection_reason). (2w)
- Phase 2 (optimization + rollout): tune smoothing windows, kv_pressure_limit, and decay constants. Add controller knobs to Console and a runtime API for per-tenant overrides. (3w)
- Phase 3 (canary): 2-node canary on Dedicated with real tenant traffic and close monitoring, rollback if tail latency regressions. (1w)

Observability and testing:
- Perf lab tests: synthetic mixes including low-QPS cold-cache tenants + spiky high-QPS tenants to simulate eviction churn.
- Integration tests: end-to-end correctness with KV eviction counters, admission logs, and per-tenant latency traces.
- Console: new dashboard panels for preservation_score, hot_fraction, kv_pressure, and mediator decisions with links to traces.

Rollout plan and rollback:
- Canary on non-critical Dedicated cluster (5% of traffic) for 48 hours. Alerting on P95/P99 regressions, evictions/sec increase > 2x, or GPU util drop > 7%. Automatic rollback to previous preemption policy if thresholds exceeded.

Open questions / risks:
- How to choose cold_threshold across heterogeneous models with different KV working-set characteristics? (Need cross-team input from model onboarding.)
- Cost accounting: should preserved KV lines billed differently? (Billing discussion in Product.)

Next steps:
- Implement Phase 1 prototype, wire basic metrics.
- Run perf lab scenarios and report microbench numbers.
